ov: Long-legged relatives of rabbits that live above ground and rely on speed, not burrows, to escape. North America’s “jackrabbits” are really hares.
rg: Native to Africa, Europe, Asia and North America, from Arctic tundra to desert edges.
df: Grasses, herbs and crops, and twigs, buds and bark in winter.

cf.tip: Rabbits are smaller, with shorter ears and legs. They live in groups in burrows, and their young are born blind and hairless.

fx: Jackrabbits can run at 65 km/h and leap 3 m in a single bound.
The spring “boxing” you see in fields is often a female fending off a male, not two males fighting.
